description: AI-generated illustrative scene, not a photograph of an actual client workshop.
prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve, photographic compositing.
EDIT IMAGE 5, the indoor conversation. Images 1–4 are original photographs of Max and are the authoritative reference for his actual appearance. The existing generated central man's face in image 5 is WRONG; do not use it as the identity reference.

Image 1 / DSC3398: strongest reference for exact face shape and facial proportions.
Image 2 / DSC3384: close, detailed three-quarter face, real glasses and natural skin.
Image 3 / DSC3596: actual seated body, head-to-shoulder-to-torso proportions, posture, white sweater.
Image 4 / DSC3817: desired natural attentive expression and head orientation: a relaxed mouth as if about to speak, engaged eyes, neutral eyebrows, no artificial smirk.
Image 5: the workshop scene to edit. Preserve its four other people, room, chairs, lighting, camera position, crop and landscape 3:2 format.

Replace the CENTRAL MAN as one coherent photographic subject, reconstructing his face, head, neck and upper body directly from the originals. His exact likeness matters more than keeping the generated pose. Preserve his real facial geometry, natural breadth of face and jaw, actual nose, eyes, forehead, light brown hair, blue glasses, subtle stubble and apparent age from images 1–2. Make him look like the very same man photographed in the workshop, not a generic similar man. Do not preserve the long narrow synthetic face, cocked head, compressed smile or artificial expression from image 5.

Use the natural forward-leaning seated posture from image 3, adapted to sitting on the existing chair, with the head more upright and naturally supported by the neck. Rebalance the head, neck, shoulder width and torso to match the ORIGINAL photographs. The head must not look miniaturized on an oversized torso; make the whole figure naturally proportional. Rebuild the whole upper body together rather than pasting a head onto the old body. Keep anatomically correct relaxed forearms and hands.

Expression is a key correction: use the relaxed, unposed, attentive face of image 4, with a softly relaxed slightly parted mouth, no tight half-smile, no one-sided grin, no raised eyebrow or squint. He is listening to the woman on the left of the scene. Natural asymmetry only, realistic eye alignment and gaze. Face identity comes from images 1–2; expression and orientation from image 4.

Keep the approved plain WHITE crewneck sweater, gently pushed-up sleeves, and jeans. Retain true photographic skin texture and the warm ambient lighting of the room; no beauty retouching, no shiny plastic skin, no stylization. Do not transfer the outdoor background. Leave all elements outside the central man's silhouette unchanged as far as possible. No text, branding or watermarks. Opaque image.
